item: The library generation's state has no lock of its own: its four names are written only inside the exclusive window, and a pin keeps every writer call there
refs: PR #1459; coordinator 17 Oct (option D of the close-window plan)
summary: library_generation guarded _GENERATION, _VALID, _WINDOW_STAMP and _DISK_CHANGED with a plain threading.Lock, _STATE. Every writer runs on the thread that holds the exclusive window and no reader ever took the lock, so it excluded nothing; its one effect was that a failed exit of a with on it (a 3-tuple allocation on 3.13) leaves it held and every later section of the same swap or the next waits behind it with the window held. The merge of the cleanup's sections left 4 of 5 (3 of 4) such sites; _STATE and its five with blocks are now gone, so a swap passes none and the failed-exit class for the state is removed, not shrunk. The proof was an inventory (writers, readers, paths outside the window); its executable form is an AST pin over src/ that fails any call of bump, disk_changing, _open_window or _close_window not inside swap_window or the body of a with ...swap_window(...) block, any store to the four names outside the writers, and any with or module-level Lock in a writer. The instruction sweep also gains a variant that calls disk_changing() in the body and asserts that after a MemoryError at any instruction of the cleanup only the new generation is valid. Red-without: a synthetic source with the lock and with a call outside the window, and a rewrite of the cleanup that decides the flag in a step of its own. The one interrupt-safety test that injected through _STATE (tests/test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py) is Q's file and changes in Q's detector PR; checked here that injecting at bump keeps it passing. Not changed: bump's two stores are not atomic against an interrupt (the lock never made them so); each server of a shared data folder has its own state and window.
